narrative.title: Cloning the Relay Team's Cross-Wired Call Sheet
narrative.scenario: A relay network stores each runner's order plus a private walkie channel that can jump to any runner — or nobody at all. The operations team needs an entirely separate clone of the network: same runner values, same handoff order, and each clone's jump channel pointing at the equivalent clone runner, never at an original. In a single weaving pass, each new runner is stitched in right behind their original; the jump channels are copied by reading the neighbour of whatever the original points at; then the weave is split back into two clean, independent chains.
narrative.inputFormat: An array pairs of n entries [value, random_index], where random_index is the 0-based position of the random target or -1 for null.
narrative.outputFormat: The deep copy expressed the same way — n pairs [value, random_index] over brand-new nodes.
constraints: random_index is -1 or an index in [0, n-1]

complexity.optimalSpace: O(n) for the n new nodes (the interleaving itself uses no map)

testCases.explanation: Every jump channel is reproduced inside the clone — e.g. the second runner's channel re-points at the clone of runner 0, never at the original.
Both channels land on the same (second) runner, and the second runner's channel loops back to itself.

hintLevels: Level 1: Two passes beat one — first invent the clone runners, then figure out where their channels point.
Level 2: Stitch each clone directly after its original; a clone's channel then mirrors its original's channel by stepping one node forward from the original's target.
Level 3: Detaching the weave needs care: un-zip alternate nodes so originals re-form their own chain while clones re-form theirs — losing either link corrupts both lists.
